architectureDecisions: Use Integration I causal reconstruction as a read-only evidence source; introduce a separate HOW-evolution boundary that owns experiment/proposal state but receives no product-acceptance authority.

Define a fixed evaluation protocol before running a candidate. It pins semantic subject, baseline, candidate, evaluator identity/policy, scenarios, evidence requirements and budgets so the candidate cannot move the goalposts.

Treat Jev as one concrete implementation of an Evaluator port via a Jev adapter. The adapter must persist exact request/response identity, model/policy identity where available, evidence bindings and freshness metadata; Jev output is evaluation evidence, not an authority shortcut.
Reuse Core verification/trust/freshness primitives to authenticate evaluator/evidence authority and reject stale evaluation inputs before any promotion proposal is actionable.
A successful evaluation yields PROPOSE_FOR_PROMOTION or KEEP_BASELINE. Only a separate independent promotion authority may publish a new current ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategy head.

Promotion reuses existing immutable strategy descriptors and CAS-fenced ExecutionPolicy current-head semantics. New attempts resolve the promoted head; existing semantic attempts keep the binding they already own.
Rollback is modeled as a new policy/head generation that selects the exact prior accepted strategy/policy refs while preserving experiment, decision and promotion history.

The research lane must determine whether the production HOW-evolution boundary should extend the existing self-upgrade pilot or be a new application module; no new generic abstraction is accepted without evidence from the current seams.
implementationSlices: J1 — Research evaluator boundary: map existing Core evaluator/trust/freshness primitives, self-upgrade pilot, Jev transport and Integration I evidence into one explicit authority diagram; decide reuse versus new HOW-evolution module.
J2 — Fixed experiment contract: define immutable semantic subject, baseline/candidate HOW pins, evaluator/policy pins, scenarios, budgets, evidence requirements and stale-input rules.
J3 — Jev adapter contract: define exact durable input/output/evidence identity, authentication/freshness behavior and failure semantics without granting mutation or acceptance authority.
J4 — Independent promotion boundary: define proposal, reviewer/authority separation, CAS currentness checks and exact policy/strategy publication semantics.
J5 — Attempt pinning and rollback: prove promoted versions only affect new attempts; recovery remains on old binding; rollback is a new auditable generation.

J6 — End-to-end proof: reconstruct one observed failure -> candidate -> Jev-backed evaluation -> independent promotion/keep-baseline -> new attempt, plus stale/race/rollback/fresh-process negative cases.
